chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: New Orleans musicians in Chicago and Los Angeles; Joe's 1923 runaway
summary: More New Orleans players were in Chicago than Los Angeles; Joe came because he had relatives here and ran away at 17 in 1923 to join the Barnes circus.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x:
You'd been gone from New Orleans. I know you
went back once in a while and all, but actually you'd been
gone working professionally out of New Orleans a whole long
while -- or Baton Rouge....

Well, like I said, I never worked around
New Orleans much.
Oh, yeah. I went back all the time.

Did you ever, in the time you were out here
first, around the time we're speaking of, '26, '27, '28...
Did you hear of any of the exploits of the New Orleans
musicians that were doing anything? Or you left them all
behind you? Or what?

Well, a big portion of the New Orleans
musicians... They had more New Orleans musicians in Chicago
at that time than they had in Los Angeles, you see. In
fact, Ram and Tudie and Ram's brother, Tubby Hall, had been
staying around Chicago. So they migrated to Los Angeles.

Well, one thing, there was always some kind of fascination about California -- although they had more music, more work in Chicago at that time, I think. What brought me to Los Angeles was just because I had wanted to come to Los Angeles. I liked it because I had my aunt and uncle living here, and I ran away from home when I was maybe 17, in 1923, and tried to join the Al G. Barnes Circus.
I remember you had said that.
But I couldn't join them, and I went up and went back home.
